summary: Considering product design consulting? Compare services, costs, models and the 11 product design partners you should shortlist in 2026.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


A product design consulting partner helps you answer what digital product to build, for whom, how it should work and how to scale. This guide covers the service types, costs and engagement models, then ranks **11 top design partners for 2026** . Superside takes the top spot, thanks to our human-led, AI-first product design approach.


**Design used to be the pretty bow added at the end of a product project. Over the last few years, that has changed.**


Digital products are now one of the main ways companies deliver value, and the quality of the experience directly influences adoption, retention and revenue. A confusing signup flow or messy dashboard doesn't just annoy users.[It quickly eats into profits.](https://www.superside.com/blog/why-design-matters)


The business case is strong. McKinsey's 2018 research on the business value of design found that top-quartile design performers achieved[32 percentage points higher revenue growth and 56 percentage points higher shareholder-return growth](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/tech-and-ai/our-insights/the-business-value-of-design) than their industry counterparts over five years, roughly twice the rate. And in PwC's 2025 Customer Experience Survey,[52% of consumers](https://www.pwc.com/us/en/services/consulting/commercial-excellence/library/2025-customer-experience-survey.html) said they'd stopped using or buying from a brand because of a bad experience with its products or services.


If you're developing a new product, **the right design consultants can help you connect product design to performance.** The best partners look beyond good-looking screens to help you make strong strategic decisions.


In this guide, we explain what product design consultants do, when external help makes sense, how the main engagement models compare and what you can expect to pay. We also rank 11 product design consulting firms for 2026 and take a closer look at why Superside leads the list.


## What is product design consulting?


A product design consulting partner provides specialized knowledge on how to build or improve digital products to make them genuinely useful, intuitive, on-brand and scalable. The discipline combines strategic direction with practical design expertise.


**The word "consulting" is important.** While a production-only team works from a defined brief and delivers the relevant screens, a consulting partner helps you work out what to build, who it's for, how it should work and what will create the most value before the design process kicks in.


A strong product design consultancy supports research, user experience (UX), user interface (UI) design, prototyping and design systems, and ties its output to a clear product and business rationale.


**Note:** *in this guide we focus on software, apps and web-based products rather than physical products or hardware design.*


The partners listed here create user flows, components, patterns, prototypes and implementation-ready documentation. They don't all turn those deliverables into code, so they're not all product development companies. We flag which is which below.


## What product design consultants do


The level of consulting you can expect will depend on your product's maturity and the problem you're trying to solve. That said, a good partner should be able to work closely with you on the following.


- **Product and design strategy.** Connecting user needs, commercial goals and technical constraints. The consultant challenges assumptions, defines priorities and helps your team agree on direction.
- **Product design audits.** A structured review identifying friction, inconsistencies, accessibility gaps and opportunities in an existing product. The outcome should be an action plan with clear priorities.
- **Research and discovery.** Interviews, usability testing, behavioral data and market research, so the product answers real user needs.
- **UX design and user flows.** Following[UX design best practices](https://www.superside.com/blog/ux-design-best-practices) to map user journeys, information architecture and interactions.
- **UI design.** The product's visual and interactive layer, from layout and hierarchy to states, components and motion.
- **Prototyping and concept validation.** Clickable prototypes so you can explore and test ideas before investing in full-scale development.
- **MVP design.** Defining and designing the smallest credible version of your product or feature, so you can validate the idea and gather real feedback.
- **Design system creation and evolution.** Reusable components, patterns, tokens and documentation to help internal and external partners maintain consistency as the product scales.
- **Developer handoff.** Specifications, component states, user flows, accessibility guidance and implementation-ready files for your engineering team.


For a fuller view of the skills involved, see our guide to the[different types of designers](https://www.superside.com/blog/different-types-of-designers) and our overview of[design strategy](https://www.superside.com/blog/design-strategy) .


## What a product design consulting process looks like


Every consultancy has a slightly different approach, but the best processes include these five steps.


Step What happens What you get


Discover the context Review of your product, concept and brand, plus research into users, business goals, analytics and technical constraints A UX or product design audit for existing products, or an opportunity map for new ones


Define the problem and priorities Research translated into a problem statement and success criteria A prioritized roadmap that says which problems are worth solving now


Explore and prototype User flows mapped, concepts developed, multiple directions tested Prototypes and a chosen direction


Validate and refine User feedback, stakeholder input and performance data applied A refined, evidence-backed design


Document and hand off Design files, specifications and system documentation prepared Enough context for your engineers to build accurately


Step two is where a consultant should earn the title. They should help you decide which problems are worth solving, which can wait and what would make for a genuinely better product.


And a good partner doesn't disappear at handoff. Expect them to make time for questions, support iteration and work closely with your team as the product nears launch.


## Why product design consulting matters: the business case


Strong design doesn't guarantee a successful product. **It does make it easier for users to understand your product's value, complete key tasks and come back.**


Beyond McKinsey's finding that design leaders outgrow their peers, more recent research helps explain the advantage. In[Maze's 2025 survey of 800 product professionals](https://maze.co/resources/user-research-report-2025/) , organizations that embedded user research into product development and decision-making reported improved usability (83%), higher customer satisfaction (63%), better product-market fit (35%) and increased customer retention (34%).


In practice, strong product design delivers value in four areas:


- **Less rework.** Good research and validation catch weak assumptions before the expensive design and development work starts.
- **Faster alignment.** A structured roadmap gives product, design, marketing and engineering a shared direction and clearer decisions.
- **Better user outcomes.** Stronger flows and interfaces improve usability, satisfaction and product-market fit, as the Maze research shows.
- **More scalable design.** Strong[design systems](https://www.superside.com/design-systems) help teams maintain consistency as the product grows across features, platforms and markets.


## When to hire a product design consultant


Some companies don't need outside help. If your in-house team has the strategy, research capability, specialist skills and capacity, it may be simplest to keep things in-house.


External support becomes genuinely valuable when one or more of these applies:


- **You're launching a new product or major feature** and want to confirm there's a real opportunity before committing a large budget.
- **You want to redesign an existing product** and need an objective audit and a clear roadmap.
- **Important metrics are moving the wrong way.** Drop-off, low adoption, a string of support tickets or poor conversion suggests the user experience needs re-evaluating.
- **Your team lacks a specialist skill.** You don't have a senior UX strategist, researcher, accessibility specialist or design system expert, and you need one for a specific project.
- **Demand has outgrown capacity.** The roadmap keeps expanding but you don't have time to hire.
- **The product has become inconsistent.** Interfaces behave differently across platforms, or nobody's sure which design system components are current.
- **Stakeholders can't agree on the problem.** You need a neutral partner to bring structure and evidence.


If the problem is purely production volume, you may need extra design capacity rather than a fully fledged consultant.


## Choose your model, in-house, consultancy or creative subscription


You can choose between three operating models. In practice, the best answer is usually a mix.


- **In-house teams** are closest to the product and the day-to-day decisions that make it a success. They're usually the right owners for the long-term roadmap. But hiring every specialist skill you'll need along the way is slow and expensive.
- **Traditional consultancies and product design agencies** bring senior expertise and a fresh perspective. They're excellent for discovery, audits and major redesigns, though they can be expensive, slow to start and disconnected from your day-to-day workflows.
- **Creative subscription partners** provide ongoing access to design capacity and specialist expertise. Superside, for example, can support[product design](https://www.superside.com/product-design) alongside[branding](https://www.superside.com/branding-services) ,[web design](https://www.superside.com/web-design-services) ,[motion](https://www.superside.com/motion-design) and[other creative needs](https://www.superside.com/design-services) . This works well when demand changes month to month, or when the product experience needs to stay connected to the broader brand.


Many organizations keep a product design lead in-house and use an external partner for audits, design systems, specialized projects and capacity surges. Our article on[choosing a design company](https://www.superside.com/blog/choosing-a-design-company) can help you weigh the options.


## How to choose a product design consulting firm


A strong portfolio can get a firm onto your longlist, but it shouldn't be the only factor. Remember, this isn't just about creating designs. Use these questions to narrow your options.


### 1. Do they understand our problem?


Look for a partner that asks about your market, product vision, business goals, constraints and success measures before talking outputs. If they jump straight to deliverables, they may be selling production capacity rather than consulting.


### 2. Can they show relevant outcomes?


Review work for similar companies, products, audiences or levels of complexity. Ask what changed because of it. A beautiful case study is useful, but evidence of better usability, adoption, conversion or speed is stronger.


### 3. Is their process clear?


Make sure you understand the stages, decision points, deliverables and roles on both sides. Ask who'll do the work, how often you'll meet and how they handle scope changes.


### 4. Can they work with our engineers?


Check where their responsibility ends. If you need designs only, ask how they document behavior, edge cases, accessibility and component states for handoff. If you also need development, confirm they provide it.


### 5. Can they support consistency at scale?


Ask how they'll use your existing[brand guidelines](https://www.superside.com/blog/branding-guide) and[design system](https://www.superside.com/blog/design-systems) . If you don't have these yet, ask whether they can build them.


### 6. Does the engagement model fit the work?


Fixed projects suit clear, bounded outcomes. Retainers and subscriptions work better for ongoing demand and roadmaps that shift. Hourly arrangements offer flexibility but require close management. Choose a model that supports both current needs and future growth.


### 7. Who owns the files and IP?


Confirm who'll own the source files, research, prototypes and design tokens. Also check which third-party fonts, images, plugins or tools carry separate licenses, since these add to the cost.


### 8. Will the relationship work in practice?


Meet the people you'll actually work with. Strong collaboration, clear communication, thoughtful pushback and shared quality standards matter more than a polished pitch.


**Last note:** before signing a contract, consider a paid pilot project such as an audit, a prototype or early testing of one feature. That gives you a realistic view of the process, the team and whether they're right for the job.


## How much does product design consulting cost?


This is hard to answer, because a product audit, a redesign, an MVP and enterprise product development are all very different jobs.


Public directories confirm the range is wide.[Clutch's 2026 product design pricing guide](https://clutch.co/agencies/product-design/pricing) puts typical projects at $10,000 to $49,999 and US agency rates at $100 to $149 per hour, while complex, senior-led enterprise work sits well outside that range.


Consultants typically price through one of four models.


Model Best for Watch out for


Hourly or day rates Consulting, workshops and evolving scopes Hard to forecast the final project cost


Fixed project fees Clearly defined audits, prototypes, MVPs or redesigns Check what's included, how many research and testing rounds are planned, and what happens when scope changes


Retainers Continuous product work with a senior consultant or team You may pay for time you don't use


Subscriptions Ongoing access to a broader creative team, especially when product design sits alongside other creative needs Confirm how capacity flexes up and down


The biggest cost drivers are research depth, the number of user groups and platforms, product complexity, design system requirements, accessibility needs, timeline, stakeholder load and whether development is included. Ask about these as you decide which model and partner to use.

### 2. IDEO


[IDEO](https://www.ideo.com/) is a global design and innovation company known for helping popularize human-centered design over nearly 50 years.


Its work combines design, systems thinking and creative experimentation across strategies, products and services. It has worked in just about every product category and counts many of the world's most innovative companies as customers.


**What sets it apart:** IDEO is strongest at the front of innovation, where the problem is ambiguous and the organization needs research, facilitation and multidisciplinary thinking to work out what to create. Worth knowing: the firm restructured significantly in 2023, cutting around a third of its headcount and closing its Munich and Tokyo studios, and now operates from five locations.


**Best for:** large organizations that want a human-centered approach to complex product design challenges.

[frog](https://www.frog.co/) , part of Capgemini Invent, is a global design and innovation consultancy working across products, services, brands and large-scale transformation. Its wider network adds technology, data and business transformation capabilities to the design offer.


**What sets it apart:** frog can connect product and service design to broader enterprise reinvention. Its scale and multidisciplinary bench suit programs spanning multiple markets, channels or business units.


**Best for:** enterprises that want an established consultancy with a human-centered approach and technology muscle behind it.


### 4. Work & Co

It works on high-profile web, mobile, commerce and platform experiences, with teams that include UX designers, product developers and other specialists.


**What sets it apart:** Work & Co is known for putting senior, hands-on product and technical talent in the same room.


**Best for:** major brands that want a flagship digital product and need both design and engineering from the same partner.


### 5. ustwo


[ustwo](https://ustwo.com/) is an employee-owned digital product studio, founded in 2004 and held by an employee ownership trust since 2022, with more than 20 years of experience taking products from discovery to launch.


Its cross-functional teams cover research, strategy, design and engineering, with a strong focus on consumer products and financial services.


**What sets it apart:** ustwo combines a people-first design culture with full delivery. Its make-test-learn approach helps teams validate ideas, refine them through research and turn them into working products.


**Best for:** organizations that want a collaborative design and development studio with strong discovery credentials.


### 6. Fantasy


[Fantasy](https://fantasy.co/) positions itself as an AI-native digital product design agency and an innovation partner to major global brands, developing enterprise-scale digital products, AI experiences and flagship consumer platforms.


**What sets it apart:** Fantasy pairs high-end interface design with product strategy and engineering. It's particularly strong when the brief calls for an ambitious, future-facing experience meant to stand out in a crowded market.


**Best for:** enterprise brands building flagship consumer products, AI experiences or category-defining platforms.


### 7. Clay


[Clay](https://clay.global/) is a San Francisco branding and UX design agency. Its services span strategic planning, research, UX and UI, prototyping, design systems, branding, web design and development.


**What sets it apart:** Clay treats brand and UX as connected disciplines, which makes it a strong option for companies refreshing a digital product and its brand identity at the same time.


**Best for:** technology companies that need a product design firm with real brand and visual identity experience. It's one of[the best UX design agencies](https://www.superside.com/blog/ux-design-agencies) around.


### 8. Ramotion


[Ramotion](https://www.ramotion.com/) is a product and brand design agency with more than 15 years of work across brand identity, marketing websites and UI and UX for web and mobile products, often for SaaS, enterprise platforms and growth-stage technology companies.


**What sets it apart:** Ramotion works at the intersection of product and brand, which is useful for teams that need a consistent identity across the interface, the marketing site and everything else.


**Best for:** growth-stage and established technology companies that need product UX, UI and branding from one agency.


### 9. Blink UX


[Blink UX](https://blinkux.com/) , an Mphasis company since 2021, is a product design firm combining strategy, research and design for organizations in technology, financial services, healthcare and other complex sectors, with AI acceleration now front and center in its pitch.


**What sets it apart:** Blink's evidence-driven approach puts research at the center of product decisions, moving quickly from concepts and customer research into experience design and validation.


**Best for:** enterprises with complex products, high research requirements or multiple stakeholder groups.


### 10. AJ&Smart


[AJ&Smart Studio](https://ajsmart.com/studio) is an independent product design and strategy studio in Berlin. The wider AJ&Smart business is best known for Design Sprints, facilitation training and structured decision-making methods.


**What sets it apart:** AJ&Smart is a strong facilitator for teams that need to align quickly, test an idea or move a stalled product decision forward. Note that the studio works by appointment and takes on client product work selectively, so treat it as a specialist engagement rather than an always-available agency.


**Best for:** focused discovery, product strategy workshops, rapid validation and teams that want to build their own facilitation capability.


### 11. Fuego UX


[Fuego UX](https://www.fuegoux.com/) is a research and design agency focused on digital products, based in Colorado with a presence in Brooklyn.


Its services include UX research, product strategy, AI design, UI design, branding, audits, prototyping, design systems, embedded talent and front-end development. It often works with B2B SaaS customers.


**What sets it apart:** Fuego combines research-led consulting with flexible embedded support, and focuses on AI-augmented experiences and complex professional workflows.


**Best for:** B2B SaaS, complex software and emerging AI products that need strong research and UX expertise.
